summary: Garden Key Light, on Fort Jefferson in the Dry Tortugas, was first lit in 1826, rebuilt in iron in 1876, discontinued in 1921 and restored in 2020-21.

corrections.why: The record's 25.0 m appears to be 25 ft converted as metres, or a different height. The USLHS record gives tower height 25 ft (about 7.6 m). Keys News gives 37 ft for the iron lighthouse structure. Editor to decide which the record should carry.
USLHS (Year Discontinued 1921), LighthouseFriends (discontinued 1921) and Rowlett all give 1921. Only the Wikidata entry gives 1924.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives 1924; USLHS, LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1921. This story uses 1921, which the Lighthouse Board's record of the automated light fits. No source read gives 1924.

NPS's fort page says the brick light was built in 1825; the NPS lighthouse page and LighthouseFriends give 1826 as the year it was completed and first exhibited. Built 1825, completed and first lit 1826.

notes_for_editor: Roster: the USLHS place Tortugas Harbor (Fort Jefferson) was matched by position (0.51 km, the only USLHS place there). The keeper lines are printed as the archive gives them (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson's inventory); not checked against the NARA registers. LighthouseFriends' description of John R. Flaherty (a 'lazy and incompetent keeper') is its own characterisation; no contemporary letter or report was read, so the story attributes it. The record's 'stay' (volunteer keeper programme) does not appear in the LighthouseFriends text read, so no stay is recorded. Tower height: the record gives 25.0 m (Wikidata); USLHS gives tower height 25 ft (7.6 m); Keys News gives a 37-foot iron lighthouse structure (not reconciled, see corrections). Discontinuance: Wikidata gives 1924; USLHS, LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1921. Searches of the Commissioner of Lighthouses reports 1915-1922 found no Garden Key discontinuance entry (OCR); the 1921 date rests on the USLHS and LighthouseFriends. Loggerhead and Garden Key: the Dry Tortugas Light on Loggerhead Key is a different station; NPS and USCG records use 'Dry Tortugas light' for it, and the 1915-1919 Commissioner entries for 'Dry Tortugas' refer to it, not to Garden Key. The story keeps them apart. Bastion: LighthouseFriends says Bastion C; a Stone and Lime project page (search snippet only, not read) says Bastion 6. Not reconciled. Construction date: NPS's fort page says the brick light was built in 1825 and LighthouseFriends says completed March 1826; the story says built 1825, first lit 1826. The 1893 characteristic change: the Lighthouse Board's OCR text is garbled after 'fixed white with'; the red sectors are from LighthouseFriends and the 1894 correction text. The 1893 shipworm entry refers to the Tortugas Harbor depot's piles (the district depot), not the light's own structure. Fire of 5 January 1912: Lighthouse Service Bulletin only (OCR); no newspaper read. The 2021 reassembly is from LighthouseFriends only; the 2020 restoration start is from LighthouseFriends and Keys News. NPS's restoration page was not found. Not read: USCG Historian archive copy (web.archive.org returned 403); NPS HDP index (404); HABS documentation on loc.gov (not located). Newspapers: Chronicling America search for 'Garden Key' 1890-1925 returned mostly 1898 items unrelated to the light; no newspaper used. Samuel Mudd and the other fort prisoners appear only as the fort's history (LighthouseFriends); the story does not connect them to the light's keepers. Record's Commons photo not reviewed for licence. Verification 2026-10-28: the 1899 upkeep figures (212 ft of brick walks, 465 ft of iron fence, the tower ironwork painted two coats) are in item 883 for Tortugas Harbor (1899 report, scan page 169); the similar sentence in item 882 concerns the Loggerhead light. The 1893 depot piles entry (1893 report, scan page 155) concerns the Tortugas Harbor depot, not the light, and was removed from the story. The 1921 discontinuance is also stated by Keys News ('deactivated in 1921'). The 1912 fire is stated in the Lighthouse Service Bulletin text ('a fire starting in an outbuilding').
